answer: Agents can bind an identity to a public-key credential and earn trust only through repeated, costly exchanges with distinct counterparties. A ledger weights each signal by the counterparty’s history, then limits how much one tightly connected island of new accounts can influence reputation. A Sybil attacker must fund many accounts and sustain credible trades with established agents; fabricated identities alone add no weight, while laundering value through a lagoon of colluding accounts remains visible in their shared connections.
